meaning: Used to say that what you predict will prove true.
japanese: よく覚えておいて、必ずそうなるから。
cue: You are confident about an unpopular prediction.
reply: Mark my words, they'll reverse this within a year.
replyJapanese: 覚えておいてください。1年以内に撤回しますよ。
transferReply: Mark my words, that hinge will go again.
transferReplyJapanese: よく見ていてください。あの蝶番はまた外れます。
nuance: Fixed with my even about others' predictions. It opens a sentence and stakes your credibility.
nuanceJapanese: 他人の予測でも my のまま。文頭に置き、自分の見立てに責任を持つ言い方。

meaning: Overcoming a physical difficulty by determination.
japanese: 気持ちの力で、体のつらさを乗り越えること。
cue: A friend is struggling in the last part of a run.
reply: The last mile is mind over matter.
replyJapanese: 最後の1マイルは、気力の勝負です。
transferReply: Getting up at five is mind over matter.
transferReplyJapanese: 5時に起きるのは、気持ちの問題です。
nuance: Fixed with no articles. It claims that will overcomes discomfort, so it can sound dismissive of real pain.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない固定表現。意志が不快に勝つという含みがあり、本当の痛みには軽く響くことがある。

meaning: Fail to understand what really matters about something.
japanese: 肝心なところを、取り違える。
cue: A reply addresses the wrong part of a question.
reply: I think that misses the point of the complaint.
replyJapanese: それは、苦情の肝心な部分を外していると思います。
transferReply: I missed the point entirely the first time.
transferReplyJapanese: 最初は、肝心なところをまるで取り違えていました。
nuance: Point takes the. About someone else it can sound sharp, so it is often softened with I think.
nuanceJapanese: point には the を付ける。他人に向けるときつく響くので、I think を添えることが多い。

meaning: Very probable.
japanese: おそらく、そうなる見込みが高い。
cue: Someone asks whether a delay will happen.
reply: It's more than likely that we'll slip a week.
replyJapanese: 1週間ずれ込む可能性が高いです。
transferReply: More than likely it'll rain by four.
transferReplyJapanese: 4時までには、おそらく雨になります。
nuance: Can open a sentence or follow it's. Stronger than likely, weaker than certain.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭にも it's のあとにも置ける。likely より強く、certain よりは弱い。

meaning: Change as the world around you changes.
japanese: 時代の変化に合わせて、自分も変わる。
cue: An organisation has kept an outdated practice.
reply: They'll have to move with the times eventually.
replyJapanese: いずれ、時代に合わせて変わらざるをえません。
transferReply: That shop has always moved with the times.
transferReplyJapanese: あの店は、いつも時代に合わせて変わってきました。
nuance: Times is always plural with the. It urges adaptation rather than criticising the past.
nuanceJapanese: times は the を伴う複数形。過去を責めるより、適応を促す表現。

meaning: Say publicly who was responsible.
japanese: 関係者の名前を、公に挙げる。
cue: A report describes a failure without identifying anyone.
reply: The report stops short of naming names.
replyJapanese: その報告書は、名指しまではしていません。
transferReply: I won't name names, but it happened twice.
transferReplyJapanese: 名前は挙げませんが、2度ありました。
nuance: Both words are the same; the second is the plural noun. Often in the negative as a discreet refusal.
nuanceJapanese: 同じ語を重ねる形で、2つ目は複数名詞。名指しを避ける断りとして、否定形で使うことが多い。

meaning: A situation where you only just avoided harm.
japanese: あやうく難を逃れたこと。
cue: A falling branch missed someone by a metre.
reply: That was a narrow escape.
replyJapanese: あやういところでした。
transferReply: We had a narrow escape at the gate.
transferReplyJapanese: 搭乗口で、ぎりぎり間に合いました。
nuance: Countable. Usually with have, and it reports relief rather than assigning blame.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞で、ふつう have と使う。責任追及ではなく、安堵を伝える。

meaning: Used before something that is obvious.
japanese: 言うまでもないことだが。
cue: An expected outcome followed from a bad decision.
reply: Needless to say, nobody was pleased.
replyJapanese: 言うまでもなく、誰も喜びませんでした。
transferReply: Needless to say, we arrived soaked.
transferReplyJapanese: 言うまでもなく、びしょ濡れで着きました。
nuance: Opens the sentence with a comma. It flags the point as expected, which can sound wry.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭にコンマを添えて置く。当然のこととして示すので、皮肉めいた響きにもなる。

meaning: Almost always.
japanese: 十中八九。たいていの場合。
cue: Describe a reliable pattern at work.
reply: Nine times out of ten it's the cable.
replyJapanese: 十中八九、原因はケーブルです。
transferReply: Nine times out of ten she takes the stairs.
transferReplyJapanese: 十中八九、彼女は階段を使います。
nuance: The numbers never change. It opens a sentence and claims a strong tendency, not certainty.
nuanceJapanese: 数字は変わらない。文頭に置き、確実さではなく強い傾向を示す。

meaning: An impressive achievement.
japanese: 並大抵ではない、立派な成果。
cue: A small team delivered something difficult.
reply: Finishing in three months was no mean feat.
replyJapanese: 3か月で仕上げたのは、並大抵のことではありません。
transferReply: Forty kilometres in a day is no mean feat.
transferReplyJapanese: 1日40キロは、たいしたものです。
nuance: Mean here means poor, so no mean feat is high praise. Always with no rather than not a.
nuanceJapanese: ここでの mean は「劣った」の意味で、no mean feat は高い評価になる。not a ではなく no を使う。

meaning: Used to add another point that strengthens your case.
japanese: 言うまでもなく、さらに。
cue: You are listing reasons against a plan.
reply: It's expensive, not to mention slow.
replyJapanese: 高いうえに、しかも遅いです。
transferReply: It saves time, not to mention paper.
transferReplyJapanese: 時間の節約になり、しかも紙も減ります。
nuance: Comes mid-sentence after a comma. It adds a point while implying it hardly needs saying.
nuanceJapanese: 文の途中にコンマを添えて置く。言うまでもないという含みで、もう一点を加える。

meaning: Not close at all to a standard or amount.
japanese: とうてい、そこには及ばない。
cue: A result fell far short of a target.
reply: We're nowhere near the target for this quarter.
replyJapanese: 今四半期の目標には、とうてい届いていません。
transferReply: An hour is nowhere near enough.
transferReplyJapanese: 1時間では、まるで足りません。
nuance: Stronger than not near. It works before nouns, adjectives and enough.
nuanceJapanese: not near より強い。名詞、形容詞、enough の前で使える。

meaning: Not allowed to be entered or discussed.
japanese: 立ち入りや言及が、禁じられている。
cue: One topic cannot be raised in a meeting.
reply: Salaries are off limits in this discussion.
replyJapanese: この議論では、給与の話は禁止です。
transferReply: The upper floor is off limits during the work.
transferReplyJapanese: 工事中、上の階は立ち入り禁止です。
nuance: Limits is always plural. Hyphenated before a noun, as in an off-limits area.
nuanceJapanese: limits はつねに複数形。名詞の前では an off-limits area のようにハイフンでつなぐ。

meaning: Not accurate.
japanese: 見当が外れている。
cue: An estimate turned out to be far from right.
reply: That forecast was well off the mark.
replyJapanese: あの予測は、大きく外れていました。
transferReply: Your guess wasn't far off the mark.
transferReplyJapanese: あなたの推測は、そう外れていませんでした。
nuance: Mark takes the. Often with well or far to show how inaccurate. On the mark is the opposite.
nuanceJapanese: mark には the を付ける。well や far を添えて、ずれの大きさを示す。反対は on the mark。

meaning: Happening sometimes, but not continuously.
japanese: 断続的に。ときどき途切れながら。
cue: Describe rain during a day out.
reply: It rained on and off all afternoon.
replyJapanese: 午後はずっと、降ったりやんだりでした。
transferReply: I've played on and off since school.
transferReplyJapanese: 学生の頃から、断続的に続けています。
nuance: Both orders are used. Comes after the verb phrase, and it stresses interruption rather than rarity.
nuanceJapanese: どちらの語順でも使う。動詞句のあとに置き、まれさより中断を強調する。

meaning: Available and ready to help if needed.
japanese: すぐ対応できるよう、控えている。
cue: Explain what support exists during an event.
reply: A technician will be on hand all day.
replyJapanese: 技術者が一日中、待機しています。
transferReply: We keep spare batteries on hand.
transferReplyJapanese: 予備の電池を、すぐ使えるようにしてあります。
nuance: Hand takes no article. Used for people who are available and for supplies kept ready.
nuanceJapanese: hand に冠詞は付かない。待機している人にも、備えてある物資にも使う。

meaning: Sometimes, but not often.
japanese: ときおり。まれにではあるが。
cue: Describe how often you work late.
reply: I stay late on occasion, not as a rule.
replyJapanese: ときおり遅くまで残りますが、いつもではありません。
transferReply: On occasion we deliver on Saturdays.
transferReplyJapanese: まれに、土曜に配送することもあります。
nuance: Occasion takes no article here. Slightly formal; occasionally is the everyday word.
nuanceJapanese: この形では occasion に冠詞は付かない。やや改まった表現で、日常では occasionally を使う。

meaning: Deliberately, not by accident.
japanese: わざと。意図的に。
cue: Someone worries a mistake looked intentional.
reply: Nobody thinks you did it on purpose.
replyJapanese: わざとやったとは、誰も思っていません。
transferReply: I left the label on purpose so you'd see it.
transferReplyJapanese: 見えるように、わざとラベルを残しておきました。
nuance: Purpose takes no article. By accident is the opposite; by purpose is not English.
nuanceJapanese: purpose に冠詞は付かない。反対は by accident で、by purpose とは言わない。

meaning: After thinking about it again.
japanese: あらためて考えてみると。
cue: You have changed your view since yesterday.
reply: On reflection, I think the first draft was better.
replyJapanese: あらためて考えると、初稿のほうがよかったと思います。
transferReply: On reflection, that was unfair of me.
transferReplyJapanese: 考え直すと、あれは私が不公平でした。
nuance: Opens the sentence with a comma. Reflection takes no article, and it signals a changed view.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭にコンマを添えて置く。reflection に冠詞は付かず、考えが変わったことを示す。

meaning: Not working properly.
japanese: 調子が悪くて、まともに動かない。
cue: An appliance is failing intermittently.
reply: The heater's been on the blink since Tuesday.
replyJapanese: 火曜から、暖房の調子が悪いです。
transferReply: The wifi is on the blink again.
transferReplyJapanese: また無線の調子が悪くなっています。
nuance: Informal and only about machines. It implies intermittent failure, not total breakdown.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、機械にのみ使う。完全な故障ではなく、断続的な不調を指す。

meaning: Very close to a major change, usually a bad one.
japanese: 大きな変化の、すぐ手前にある。
cue: An organisation may not survive the month.
reply: The company is on the brink of closing.
replyJapanese: その会社は、閉鎖の瀬戸際にあります。
transferReply: They were on the brink of a breakthrough.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは、大きな発見の一歩手前にいました。
frame: Be on the brink of something
nuance: Of introduces what is about to happen. Usually negative, though a breakthrough works too.
nuanceJapanese: 起きようとしていることは of で示す。ふつうは否定的だが、breakthrough のような語とも使える。

meaning: Used to state the opposite of what was just said.
japanese: それどころか、まったく逆で。
cue: Someone assumes you disliked something you loved.
reply: On the contrary, I thought it was excellent.
replyJapanese: それどころか、素晴らしいと思いました。
transferReply: On the contrary, it saved us money.
transferReplyJapanese: むしろ逆で、費用の節約になりました。
nuance: Opens the sentence. It contradicts what was just said; in contrast merely compares two things.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置く。直前の発言を否定する。単に比較する in contrast とは異なる。

meaning: Forced to defend yourself against criticism.
japanese: 批判に対して、守勢に立たされている。
cue: A colleague reacted defensively to a question.
reply: He went on the defensive straight away.
replyJapanese: 彼はすぐに守勢に回りました。
transferReply: Try not to put them on the defensive.
transferReplyJapanese: 相手を守勢に追い込まないようにしましょう。
nuance: Defensive takes the. Used with be, go or put someone, and it describes a posture, not a feeling.
nuanceJapanese: defensive には the を付ける。be、go、put someone と使い、感情ではなく姿勢を表す。

meaning: Becoming more frequent or larger.
japanese: 増加傾向にある。
cue: A figure has risen steadily. Report it.
reply: Complaints have been on the increase since March.
replyJapanese: 3月以降、苦情は増加傾向にあります。
transferCue: Describe a trend in a report.
transferReply: Cycling is on the increase in the city.
transferReplyJapanese: 市内では、自転車の利用が増えています。
nuance: Increase takes the. On the rise means the same and is slightly more common in speech.
nuanceJapanese: increase には the を付ける。on the rise も同じ意味で、会話ではやや一般的。

meaning: Travelling, or changing position constantly.
japanese: 移動中である。絶えず動いている。
cue: Explain why you are hard to reach today.
reply: I'm on the move all day, so email is better.
replyJapanese: 今日は一日移動中なので、メールのほうが確実です。
transferReply: The whole sector is on the move again.
transferReplyJapanese: 業界全体が、また動き始めています。
nuance: Move takes the. Two senses: physically travelling, and changing or developing.
nuanceJapanese: move には the を付ける。「移動中」と「変化している」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Used to introduce a contrasting point.
japanese: 一方で、別の見方をすれば。
cue: You are weighing two sides of a decision.
reply: It's cheaper. On the other hand, delivery takes a month.
replyJapanese: 安くはあります。一方で、配送に1か月かかります。
transferReply: On the other hand, we'd learn a lot.
transferReplyJapanese: 一方で、学べることは多いでしょう。
nuance: Opens a sentence. It usually follows on the one hand, though that half is often left out.
nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置く。on the one hand に続くのがふつうだが、前半は省かれることも多い。

meaning: Just about to do something.
japanese: まさに、しようとしているところ。
cue: You almost left before someone arrived.
reply: I was on the point of leaving when she called.
replyJapanese: 帰ろうとしたちょうどそのとき、彼女から電話がありました。
transferReply: We were on the point of cancelling the whole thing.
transferReplyJapanese: すべて取りやめる寸前でした。
frame: Be on the point of doing something
nuance: Followed by -ing, never by to. Point takes the, and it usually describes a moment interrupted.
nuanceJapanese: -ing を続け、to は使わない。point には the を付け、中断された瞬間を表すことが多い。

meaning: Secretly, without telling people.
japanese: 人に知らせず、こっそりと。
cue: Someone has been doing something without announcing it.
reply: He's been studying on the quiet for a year.
replyJapanese: 彼は1年、こっそり勉強を続けていました。
transferReply: We booked it on the quiet.
transferReplyJapanese: 内緒で予約しておきました。
nuance: British and informal. Quiet takes the here, unlike the adjective.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。形容詞と違い、ここでは quiet に the を付ける。

meaning: In addition to your main job or as an extra.
japanese: 本業のかたわらで。また、添え物として。
cue: Someone does paid work outside their main role.
reply: She does translation on the side.
replyJapanese: 彼女は本業のかたわら、翻訳もしています。
transferReply: Could I have the dressing on the side?
transferReplyJapanese: ドレッシングは別添えでお願いできますか。
nuance: Side takes the. Two senses: extra work, and food served separately.
nuanceJapanese: side には the を付ける。「副業」と「別添え」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Occasionally.
japanese: たまに。ときどき。
cue: Describe how often you eat out.
reply: We go out once in a while, not every week.
replyJapanese: 毎週ではありませんが、たまに外食します。
transferReply: Once in a while you should take the whole day off.
transferReplyJapanese: たまには、まる一日休むべきです。
nuance: Often with every. Less frequent than sometimes but more than once in a blue moon.
nuanceJapanese: every を添えることが多い。sometimes より少なく、once in a blue moon よりは多い。

meaning: Exactly the same person or thing.
japanese: まったく同一のものである。
cue: Two names turn out to refer to one person.
reply: The author and the illustrator are one and the same.
replyJapanese: 著者と挿絵画家は、同一人物です。
transferCue: Clarify two labels for one thing.
transferReply: The two departments are one and the same now.
transferReplyJapanese: その2つの部署は、今は同じひとつです。
nuance: Fixed word order. It identifies two references as a single thing, not merely as similar.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定。似ているのではなく、二つの呼び名が同一のものだと示す。

meaning: A day when everything seems to go wrong.
japanese: 何をしてもうまくいかない日。
cue: Three small things have gone wrong before lunch.
reply: It's just one of those days.
replyJapanese: 今日はそういう日みたいです。
transferCue: Explain a short temper to a colleague.
transferReply: Sorry, I'm having one of those days.
transferReplyJapanese: すみません、今日はそういう日で。
nuance: Those is fixed and refers to a known kind of bad day. Usually said with resignation.
nuanceJapanese: those は固定で、よくある「ついていない日」を指す。あきらめ気味に言うことが多い。

meaning: Something supposedly secret that everyone knows.
japanese: 秘密のはずが、みんな知っていること。
cue: An unannounced departure is widely known.
reply: His leaving is an open secret by now.
replyJapanese: 彼が辞めることは、もう公然の秘密です。
transferReply: The new model is an open secret in the trade.
transferReplyJapanese: 新型のことは、業界では公然の秘密です。
nuance: Countable. The contradiction is the point: it is formally secret and generally known.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞。建前は秘密、実際は周知という矛盾がこの表現の要点。

meaning: Going out and doing things, especially after being unable to.
japanese: 外に出て、動き回っている。
cue: A friend has recovered from an illness.
reply: It's good to see you out and about again.
replyJapanese: また元気に出歩けるようになって、よかったです。
transferReply: I've been out and about since seven.
transferReplyJapanese: 7時から、あちこち出歩いています。
nuance: Fixed word order. It often implies a return to activity after illness or bad weather.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定。病気や悪天候のあと、また動けるようになった含みを持つことが多い。

meaning: Outside the area or subject that is permitted.
japanese: 許された範囲の外にある。
cue: A part of a site cannot be entered.
reply: The yard is out of bounds to visitors.
replyJapanese: その構内は、来訪者は立ち入り禁止です。
transferCue: Describe a topic that is off the table.
transferReply: Personal finances are out of bounds here.
transferReplyJapanese: ここでは、個人の財務は触れてはいけない話題です。
frame: Be out of bounds to someone
nuance: Bounds is always plural. To introduces who is excluded. Common on signs and in sport.
nuanceJapanese: bounds はつねに複数形。対象は to で示す。掲示やスポーツでよく使う。

meaning: Not able to be used or to work.
japanese: 使えない状態になっている。
cue: A vehicle is being repaired.
reply: The van is out of commission until Thursday.
replyJapanese: そのバンは木曜まで、使えません。
transferReply: A bad back had him out of commission for a week.
transferReplyJapanese: 腰痛で、彼は1週間動けませんでした。
nuance: Commission takes no article. Used for machines and, lightly, for people who are unwell.
nuanceJapanese: commission に冠詞は付かない。機械のほか、体調を崩した人にも軽く使う。

meaning: In a safe place, away from danger.
japanese: 危険の及ばない、安全なところに。
cue: You are moving something breakable before a party.
reply: Let's put the vase out of harm's way.
replyJapanese: 花瓶は、安全なところに移しましょう。
transferReply: The tools are kept out of harm's way.
transferReplyJapanese: 工具は、危険のない場所にしまってあります。
frame: Put something out of harm's way
nuance: Fixed with the possessive harm's. It means away from danger, not away from doing harm.
nuanceJapanese: harm's の所有格を含む固定表現。害を与えないのではなく、害が及ばないという意味。

meaning: Unable to get what you wanted.
japanese: 運悪く、望みがかなわない。
cue: The last of something has just been sold.
reply: You're out of luck — the last one went this morning.
replyJapanese: あいにくですが、最後の1点は今朝売れました。
transferReply: We were out of luck by ten minutes.
transferReplyJapanese: 10分の差で、間に合いませんでした。
nuance: Luck takes no article. It reports an unlucky outcome without blaming anyone.
nuanceJapanese: luck に冠詞は付かない。誰も責めずに、運の悪い結果を伝える。

meaning: Not suitable for the situation, or not in the right position.
japanese: その場にそぐわない。あるべき位置にない。
cue: You wore casual clothes to a formal event.
reply: I felt completely out of place in jeans.
replyJapanese: ジーンズ姿で、すっかり場違いに感じました。
transferReply: Not one thing was out of place.
transferReplyJapanese: ひとつとして、乱れたところがありませんでした。
nuance: Place takes no article. Two senses: socially unsuitable, and physically misplaced.
nuanceJapanese: place に冠詞は付かない。「場違い」と「位置がずれている」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Not as skilled as before because you have not done it recently.
japanese: しばらくやっていなくて、腕が鈍っている。
cue: You have not played an instrument for years.
reply: I'm badly out of practice on the piano.
replyJapanese: ピアノは、すっかり腕が鈍っています。
transferReply: She's out of practice but it came back quickly.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は腕が鈍っていましたが、すぐ勘を取り戻しました。
nuance: Practice takes no article. It blames the gap, not the ability. In practice means the opposite here.
nuanceJapanese: practice に冠詞は付かない。能力ではなく、間が空いたことを理由にする。反対は in practice。

meaning: Not at the time of year when something is usual or available.
japanese: 時期外れで、旬ではない。
cue: A fruit is expensive at this time of year.
reply: Strawberries are out of season and cost a fortune.
replyJapanese: いちごは時期外れで、非常に高いです。
transferReply: The town is lovely out of season.
transferReplyJapanese: その町は、観光の時期を外すと素敵です。
nuance: Season takes no article. Used for food and for tourist periods. In season is the opposite.
nuanceJapanese: season に冠詞は付かない。食材にも観光の時期にも使う。反対は in season。

meaning: Where it cannot be seen.
japanese: 見えないところに。
cue: You are hiding a present before a birthday.
reply: Keep it out of sight until Saturday.
replyJapanese: 土曜までは、見えないところにしまっておいてください。
transferReply: It was out of sight within ten minutes.
transferReplyJapanese: 10分で、見えなくなりました。
nuance: Sight takes no article. The proverb out of sight, out of mind is a separate fixed phrase.
nuanceJapanese: sight に冠詞は付かない。ことわざ out of sight, out of mind は別の固定表現。

meaning: Not blocking anything, or finished and dealt with.
japanese: 邪魔にならない位置に。また、片づいて。
cue: A task is finished and you can move on.
reply: With that out of the way, we can start the design.
replyJapanese: それが片づいたので、設計に入れます。
transferReply: Could you move the boxes out of the way?
transferReplyJapanese: 箱をどけてもらえますか。
frame: Get something out of the way
nuance: Way takes the. Two senses: physically clear, and completed. Out-of-the-way also means remote.
nuanceJapanese: way には the を付ける。「どける」と「片づける」の2つの意味がある。out-of-the-way は「へんぴな」の意味にもなる。

meaning: Repeatedly, many times.
japanese: 何度も繰り返して。
cue: A child wants the same story again.
reply: She reads it over and over.
replyJapanese: 彼女は同じ本を、何度も読み返します。
transferReply: I played the passage over and over until it worked.
transferReplyJapanese: うまくいくまで、その箇所を何度も弾きました。
nuance: Often extended with again. It stresses repetition, sometimes with a hint of tedium.
nuanceJapanese: again を添えることも多い。繰り返しを強調し、うんざり感を含むこともある。

meaning: Too old to do something as well as before.
japanese: 盛りを過ぎて、以前ほどではない。
cue: Someone jokes about their own age at a race.
reply: I'm over the hill for sprinting, but I can still walk far.
replyJapanese: 短距離はもう無理ですが、長く歩くことはできます。
transferReply: Forty isn't over the hill by any measure.
transferReplyJapanese: 40歳は、どう見ても盛りを過ぎた年ではありません。
nuance: Informal and usually teasing. Said about someone else it can offend, so it suits self-deprecation.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた、ふつうはからかいの表現。他人に言うと失礼になりうるので、自嘲向き。

meaning: Have a strong effect.
japanese: 見た目以上に、効き目が強い。
cue: A small dish turned out to be very spicy.
reply: That sauce packs a punch.
replyJapanese: あのソースは、なかなか効きます。
transferCue: Describe a short but powerful speech.
transferReply: Her three minutes packed a punch.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女の3分間は、強く印象に残りました。
nuance: Informal. Often with real for emphasis. Used for flavour, arguments and performances.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現。強調のため real を添えることが多い。味にも論旨にも演技にも使う。

meaning: Do something to make waiting less boring.
japanese: 退屈な時間を、何かをして紛らす。
cue: You are waiting for a delayed train.
reply: I read a magazine to pass the time.
replyJapanese: 時間をつぶすため、雑誌を読みました。
transferReply: We played cards to pass the time.
transferReplyJapanese: 時間をつぶすため、トランプをしました。
frame: Do something to pass the time
nuance: Time takes the. Pass the time of day with someone is a separate phrase meaning chat briefly.
nuanceJapanese: time には the を付ける。pass the time of day with someone は「短く世間話をする」という別の表現。

meaning: Go to see someone or something.
japanese: 訪ねていく。立ち寄る。
cue: You plan to see a relative this weekend.
reply: I'll pay a visit to my aunt on Sunday.
replyJapanese: 日曜に、叔母を訪ねるつもりです。
transferReply: It's worth paying a visit to the gallery.
transferReplyJapanese: あの美術館は、一度訪れる価値があります。
nuance: The person goes between pay and a. Slightly formal; visit is also fine as a plain verb.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は pay と a のあいだに置く。やや改まった表現で、動詞 visit でも言える。

meaning: Earn your position by doing the hard, unglamorous work first.
japanese: 下積みを経て、立場を得る。
cue: Someone was promoted after years of routine work.
reply: She paid her dues before she led anything.
replyJapanese: 彼女は率いる立場になる前に、下積みを重ねました。
transferReply: Everyone pays their dues in the first year.
transferReplyJapanese: 最初の1年は、誰もが下積みを経験します。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and dues is always plural. It implies the effort was deserved.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、dues はつねに複数形。その苦労が当然だったという含みがある。

meaning: Deliberately start an argument.
japanese: わざと、けんかを売る。
cue: Someone is being provocative in a meeting.
reply: He seems to be picking a fight over nothing.
replyJapanese: 彼は何でもないことで、けんかを売っているようです。
transferReply: Don't pick a fight you can't win.
transferReplyJapanese: 勝てないけんかは、売らないほうがいいです。
nuance: With introduces the other person. It implies the fight was deliberately started, not stumbled into.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は with で示す。偶然ではなく、意図的に始めたことを含意する。

meaning: Depend entirely on one thing working out.
japanese: 望みを、そのひとつに託す。
cue: A team is relying on a single outcome.
reply: We've pinned our hopes on the spring order.
replyJapanese: 春の受注に、望みを託しています。
transferReply: Don't pin your hopes on one interview.
transferReplyJapanese: 面接ひとつに、望みを託さないでください。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and hopes is always plural. It warns of over-reliance.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、hopes はつねに複数形。頼りすぎへの注意を含む。

meaning: Contribute to causing something.
japanese: その一因として、関わる。
cue: Several factors contributed to a result.
reply: The weather played a part in the delay.
replyJapanese: 遅延には、天候も一因として関わっています。
transferReply: Everyone played a part in getting it finished.
transferReplyJapanese: 仕上げるうえで、全員が役割を果たしました。
nuance: In introduces the result. Play a role in means the same and is slightly more formal.
nuanceJapanese: 結果は in で示す。play a role in も同じ意味で、やや改まった響き。

meaning: Behave honestly and according to the rules.
japanese: 正々堂々と、公平にふるまう。
cue: Someone is bending the rules in a game.
reply: Play fair — you moved twice.
replyJapanese: 正々堂々とやりましょう。2回動かしましたよ。
transferReply: They didn't play fair over the tender.
transferReplyJapanese: 入札について、彼らは公正ではありませんでした。
nuance: Fair is an adverb here, so it is not playing fairly in this fixed phrase.
nuanceJapanese: ここでの fair は副詞で、この固定表現では playing fairly とは言わない。

meaning: Cause serious disruption to something.
japanese: めちゃくちゃに混乱させる。
cue: Bad weather disrupted a whole timetable.
reply: The snow played havoc with the schedule.
replyJapanese: 雪が、日程をめちゃくちゃにしました。
transferReply: Shift work plays havoc with your sleep.
transferReplyJapanese: 交代勤務は、睡眠を大きく乱します。
nuance: Havoc takes no article. Wreak havoc is a stronger variant. The cause is the subject.
nuanceJapanese: havoc に冠詞は付かない。より強い言い方は wreak havoc。主語は原因のほう。

meaning: Directly and without any softening.
japanese: なんの前置きもなく、単刀直入に。
cue: Someone refused without explanation.
reply: She refused point blank.
replyJapanese: 彼女はきっぱりと断りました。
transferReply: He asked point blank whether we were leaving.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は単刀直入に、辞めるのかと聞いてきました。
nuance: Follows the verb. Point-blank with a hyphen goes before a noun, as in a point-blank refusal.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞のあとに置く。名詞の前では a point-blank refusal のようにハイフンでつなぐ。

meaning: Ask someone to marry you.
japanese: 結婚を申し込む。
cue: A friend is planning a proposal.
reply: He's going to pop the question in Kyoto.
replyJapanese: 彼は京都で、結婚を申し込むつもりです。
transferCue: Describe how a couple got engaged.
transferReply: She popped the question on a walk.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は散歩の途中で、結婚を申し込みました。
nuance: Question takes the. Informal and light, and it refers only to a marriage proposal.
nuanceJapanese: question には the を付ける。くだけた軽い表現で、結婚の申し込みにのみ使う。

meaning: Do yourself what you tell others to do.
japanese: 人に説くことを、自分でも実行する。
cue: Someone advises a habit they do not follow.
reply: It's easier to preach than to practise what you preach.
replyJapanese: 説くのは簡単ですが、自分で実行するのは難しいものです。
transferReply: She practises what she preaches about hours.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は勤務時間について、自ら言うとおりに実行しています。
nuance: British spells the verb practise; American practice. Often used to point out inconsistency.
nuanceJapanese: 動詞はイギリス英語で practise、アメリカ英語で practice。言行不一致を指摘するのに使うことが多い。

meaning: Do the preliminary work that makes something possible.
japanese: 実現に向けて、下地を整える。
cue: Early conversations made a later decision easy.
reply: Those meetings prepared the ground for the merger.
replyJapanese: あの会合が、合併への下地を整えました。
transferReply: We prepared the ground before announcing it.
transferReplyJapanese: 発表の前に、周囲の下地を整えておきました。
nuance: Ground takes the. For introduces what follows. Lay the groundwork means the same.
nuanceJapanese: ground には the を付ける。続くことは for で示す。lay the groundwork も同じ意味。

meaning: Make something end.
japanese: やめさせて、終わりにする。
cue: A harmful practice needs to end.
reply: We need to put a stop to the late changes.
replyJapanese: 直前の変更は、やめさせる必要があります。
transferReply: The new gate put a stop to the shortcut.
transferReplyJapanese: 新しい門ができて、抜け道は使えなくなりました。
nuance: Stop takes a. It implies authority to end something, not merely wanting it to end.
nuanceJapanese: stop には a を付ける。終わってほしいのではなく、終わらせる力があることを含意する。

meaning: Say something helpful about someone to a person with influence.
japanese: 口添えをして、よい話をしておく。
cue: A friend is applying where you have contacts.
reply: I'll put in a word with the manager.
replyJapanese: 店長に、ひとこと口添えしておきます。
transferReply: Thanks for putting in a word for me.
transferReplyJapanese: 口添えしてくださって、ありがとうございました。
frame: Put in a good word for someone
nuance: Often with good. For introduces who benefits, with introduces who you speak to.
nuanceJapanese: good を添えることが多い。恩恵を受ける人は for、話す相手は with で示す。

meaning: Start actually doing what was planned or learned.
japanese: 計画や学びを、実際に行動に移す。
cue: Training has finished and work begins.
reply: Now we put the training into practice.
replyJapanese: ここからは、研修の内容を実践に移します。
transferReply: She put the advice into practice immediately.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はその助言を、すぐ実践に移しました。
nuance: The object goes between put and into. Practice takes no article here.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は put と into のあいだに置く。ここでの practice に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Show how important something really is by comparison.
japanese: 比べることで、本当の重要度を分からせる。
cue: A small complaint follows news of something serious.
reply: That rather puts our problems into perspective.
replyJapanese: それを聞くと、こちらの悩みは小さく思えます。
transferReply: One number puts the whole budget into perspective.
transferReplyJapanese: その数字ひとつで、予算全体の大きさが分かります。
nuance: The object goes between put and into. Perspective takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は put と into のあいだに置く。perspective に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Start writing something.
japanese: 実際に、書き始める。
cue: Someone has been planning to write for months.
reply: He finally put pen to paper in January.
replyJapanese: 彼は1月に、ようやく書き始めました。
transferReply: It took me a week to put pen to paper.
transferReplyJapanese: 書き始めるまでに、1週間かかりました。
nuance: No articles inside the phrase. Used even when the writing is done on a screen.
nuanceJapanese: 句の中に冠詞は入らない。画面で書く場合にも使う。

meaning: Be so much better that the other thing looks poor.
japanese: 引き比べて、見劣りさせてしまう。
cue: An amateur effort was better than a professional one.
reply: Her cake puts the bakery to shame.
replyJapanese: 彼女のケーキは、あのパン屋が見劣りするほどです。
transferReply: The junior team put the seniors to shame.
transferReplyJapanese: 下級生のチームが、上級生を圧倒しました。
nuance: The object goes between put and to. Shame takes no article. It compliments by comparison.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は put と to のあいだに置く。shame に冠詞は付かない。比較によってほめる表現。

meaning: Resist strongly instead of giving in.
japanese: 簡単には引き下がらず、抵抗する。
cue: A team lost but made it difficult.
reply: They lost, but they put up a fight.
replyJapanese: 負けはしましたが、彼らはよく抵抗しました。
transferReply: The residents put up a fight over the closure.
transferReplyJapanese: 住民は閉鎖に対して、強く抵抗しました。
nuance: Fight takes a. Usually admiring of the resistance, even when it fails.
nuanceJapanese: fight には a を付ける。失敗した場合でも、抵抗を肯定的に評価することが多い。

meaning: Do something with full commitment and feeling.
japanese: 心を込めて、全力で取り組む。
cue: Someone worked on something with real care.
reply: She put her heart into that garden.
replyJapanese: 彼女はあの庭に、心を込めていました。
transferReply: Put your heart into it and it'll show.
transferReplyJapanese: 心を込めれば、それは伝わります。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It describes emotional commitment, not just hard work.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。単なる労力ではなく、気持ちの込め方を表す。

meaning: Start performing at a higher level.
japanese: 一段上の水準に、自分を引き上げる。
cue: Standards have risen and the team must respond.
reply: We'll have to raise our game next season.
replyJapanese: 来季は、もう一段上を目指す必要があります。
transferReply: He raised his game after the first review.
transferReplyJapanese: 最初の評価のあと、彼は一段上の働きを見せました。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Up your game means the same and is more informal.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。up your game も同じ意味で、よりくだけた言い方。

meaning: Come together to support someone in difficulty.
japanese: 困っている人のために、みんなで力を合わせる。
cue: A neighbour had an accident and got help.
reply: The whole street rallied round after the fire.
replyJapanese: 火事のあと、通りじゅうが力を合わせました。
transferReply: The team rallied round while she was away.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女の不在中、チームが結束して支えました。
nuance: British uses round, American around. It describes a group, not one helper.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語は round、アメリカ英語は around。一人ではなく、集団の支援を表す。

meaning: Study a subject by reading about it.
japanese: 本や資料を読んで、下調べする。
cue: You need background before a meeting.
reply: I'll read up on the regulations tonight.
replyJapanese: 今夜、規制について調べておきます。
transferReply: She read up on the area before going.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は行く前に、その地域について調べました。
nuance: Inseparable; on introduces the subject. It implies deliberate preparation.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、対象は on で示す。意識的な準備であることを含意する。

meaning: Experience the results of your own earlier actions.
japanese: 自分のまいた種を、自分で刈り取る。
cue: Earlier carelessness has caused a problem.
reply: We're reaping what we sowed last summer.
replyJapanese: 去年の夏にまいた種を、今刈り取っています。
transferCue: Describe a positive result of effort.
transferReply: She's reaping what she sowed over ten years.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は10年かけてまいた種を、今刈り取っています。
nuance: Sow is irregular: sowed, sown. Usually about bad consequences, though it works for good ones.
nuanceJapanese: sow は不規則変化で sowed、sown。ふつうは悪い結果だが、よい結果にも使える。

meaning: Bring something under control.
japanese: 手綱を引いて、抑え込む。
cue: Spending has grown beyond plan.
reply: We need to rein in the travel budget.
replyJapanese: 出張費を、抑え込む必要があります。
transferReply: He reined in his ambitions for a year.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は1年、野心を抑えました。
nuance: Separable: rein it in. Spelled rein, from horse riding, not reign.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：rein it in。つづりは reign ではなく rein で、乗馬に由来する。

meaning: Refuse to be affected by something petty.
japanese: くだらないことに、乗らずにいる。
cue: Someone is being provoked online.
reply: It's better to rise above it and say nothing.
replyJapanese: 相手にせず、何も言わないほうがいいです。
transferReply: She rose above the criticism entirely.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女はその批判に、まったく動じませんでした。
nuance: Rise is irregular: rose, risen. It praises restraint, not indifference.
nuanceJapanese: rise は不規則変化で rose、risen。無関心ではなく、自制をほめる表現。

meaning: Completely reliable or firm.
japanese: びくともしないほど、確かである。
cue: Evidence for a claim is very strong.
reply: The data behind this is rock solid.
replyJapanese: これを支えるデータは、非常に確かです。
transferReply: He's been rock solid all through the project.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はこの企画の間ずっと、頼りになりました。
nuance: Hyphenated before a noun. Used for evidence, structures and people alike.
nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前ではハイフンでつなぐ。証拠にも構造物にも人にも使う。

meaning: Get ready to do hard work.
japanese: 腕まくりして、本気で取りかかる。
cue: A big clear-out is about to start.
reply: Let's roll up our sleeves and start with the shed.
replyJapanese: 腕まくりして、まず物置から始めましょう。
transferReply: She rolled up her sleeves and helped carry boxes.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は腕まくりして、箱運びを手伝いました。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and sleeves is plural. It signals willingness, not just effort.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、sleeves は複数形。労力だけでなく、進んで取り組む姿勢を示す。

meaning: Simple and not refined, but good enough.
japanese: 作りは粗いが、用は足りる。
cue: A quick prototype is being shown.
reply: It's rough and ready, but it shows the idea.
replyJapanese: 粗い作りですが、考えは伝わります。
transferReply: Supper was rough and ready and very good.
transferReplyJapanese: 夕食は簡素でしたが、とてもおいしかったです。
nuance: Fixed word order. It excuses the roughness by pointing at usefulness.
nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定。粗さを、実用性で埋め合わせる言い方。

meaning: Keep reminding someone of something embarrassing.
japanese: 失敗を、何度も蒸し返して追い打ちをかける。
cue: A friend keeps mentioning your mistake.
reply: All right, you don't have to rub it in.
replyJapanese: 分かりましたから、何度も言わないでください。
transferReply: They won and then rubbed it in all evening.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは勝ったうえに、一晩中それを言い続けました。
nuance: Fixed with it. Informal, and usually said in protest by the person being teased.
nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。くだけた言い方で、からかわれる側が抗議として使うことが多い。

meaning: Control a group very strictly.
japanese: 鉄の規律で、厳しく支配する。
cue: Describe a very strict former manager.
reply: He ruled with an iron fist for a decade.
replyJapanese: 彼は10年間、鉄の規律で組織を治めました。
transferReply: She doesn't rule with an iron fist, and it works.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は力で押さえつけませんが、それでうまくいっています。
aliases: rule with a rod of iron
nuance: British also says with a rod of iron. Always critical of the severity.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では with a rod of iron とも言う。その厳しさへの批判をつねに含む。

meaning: Avoid something because it frightens you.
japanese: 怖くて、逃げ出したくなる。
cue: Someone dislikes public speaking intensely.
reply: He'd run a mile rather than give a speech.
replyJapanese: 彼は挨拶をするくらいなら、逃げ出すでしょう。
transferReply: Mention a two-year contract and she'd run a mile.
transferReplyJapanese: 2年契約と言えば、彼女は逃げ出すでしょう。
nuance: Usually with would. It exaggerates the reluctance rather than describing real running.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう would と使う。実際に走るのではなく、嫌がり方を誇張する表現。

meaning: Be felt very strongly, below the surface.
japanese: 表には出ないが、根が深い。
cue: An old disagreement still affects a group.
reply: The resentment runs deep in that team.
replyJapanese: あのチームでは、わだかまりが根深く残っています。
transferReply: Loyalty runs deep in that family.
transferReplyJapanese: あの家族には、深い結束があります。
nuance: The feeling is the subject. Deep is an adverb here, not deeply.
nuanceJapanese: 主語は感情のほう。ここでの deep は副詞で、deeply とは言わない。

meaning: Have almost none of something left.
japanese: 残りが少なくなる。
cue: Supplies are nearly gone before the end of a week.
reply: We're running short of paper again.
replyJapanese: また紙が足りなくなってきました。
transferReply: We ran short of time at the end.
transferReplyJapanese: 最後は、時間が足りなくなりました。
nuance: Of introduces what is nearly gone. Run out of means it has finished completely.
nuanceJapanese: 不足しているものは of で示す。完全になくなった場合は run out of を使う。

meaning: Only just succeed in passing something.
japanese: ぎりぎりで、なんとか通る。
cue: An exam result was barely a pass.
reply: I scraped through the second paper.
replyJapanese: 2科目めは、ぎりぎりで通りました。
transferReply: They scraped through to the final round.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らはぎりぎりで、決勝に進みました。
nuance: Intransitive or with an object. It reports a narrow pass, which can sound modest or relieved.
nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でも目的語付きでも使う。かろうじての合格を表し、謙遜や安堵の響きになる。

meaning: Be published, released or brought into use.
japanese: 世に出る。日の目を見る。
cue: A project was finished but never released.
reply: That design never saw the light of day.
replyJapanese: あの設計は、ついに日の目を見ませんでした。
transferReply: The manuscript finally saw the light of day in 2024.
transferReplyJapanese: その原稿は2024年に、ようやく世に出ました。
nuance: See is irregular: saw, seen. Often in the negative about work that was shelved.
nuanceJapanese: see は不規則変化で saw、seen。棚上げされた仕事について、否定形で使うことが多い。

meaning: Be useful for something.
japanese: 何らかの役に立っている。
cue: An odd-looking rule turns out to be useful.
reply: The extra check does serve a purpose.
replyJapanese: あの追加確認にも、ちゃんと意味があります。
transferReply: I'm not sure this form serves any purpose.
transferReplyJapanese: この書式に、意味があるとは思えません。
nuance: Purpose takes a, or any in the negative. It defends or questions usefulness.
nuanceJapanese: purpose には a を付け、否定形では any を使う。有用性を擁護、または疑う表現。

meaning: Do something that others may later point to as an example.
japanese: 前例を作る。
cue: An exception could be used to justify future requests.
reply: Approving this sets a precedent we'd regret.
replyJapanese: これを認めれば、後悔する前例を作ることになります。
transferReply: The ruling set a precedent for similar cases.
transferReplyJapanese: あの判決は、同種の事案の前例となりました。
nuance: Set is irregular and unchanged: set. For introduces what follows, and it often warns.
nuanceJapanese: set は不規則変化で形が変わらない。続くものは for で示し、警告として使うことが多い。

meaning: See someone or something for the first time.
japanese: 初めて目にする。
cue: Describe a first impression from years ago.
reply: I knew from the moment I set eyes on it.
replyJapanese: ひと目見た瞬間から、分かっていました。
transferReply: I'd never set eyes on the place before.
transferReplyJapanese: その場所を目にするのは、初めてでした。
nuance: Eyes is always plural. Usually with first, never or the moment, and set never changes.
nuanceJapanese: eyes はつねに複数形。first、never、the moment と使うことが多く、set は形が変わらない。

meaning: Start a process that then continues.
japanese: 動き出す仕組みを、始動させる。
cue: A decision triggered a series of steps.
reply: That signature set the whole process in motion.
replyJapanese: あの署名が、一連の手続きを動かし始めました。
transferReply: We set the application in motion in March.
transferReplyJapanese: 3月に、申請の手続きを動かし始めました。
nuance: The object goes between set and in. Motion takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: 目的語は set と in のあいだに置く。motion に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Support something that is becoming weak.
japanese: 弱ってきたものを、下支えする。
cue: A struggling part of a business needs help.
reply: The loan shores up the business until spring.
replyJapanese: その融資が、春まで事業を下支えします。
transferReply: Two more examples would shore up the case.
transferReplyJapanese: 例をあと2つ足せば、論拠が固まります。
nuance: Separable: shore it up. From building work, and it implies the thing was weakening.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：shore it up。建築由来で、弱ってきていたことを含意する。

meaning: Next to each other, or working together.
japanese: 並んで。また、協力し合って。
cue: Describe how two people worked on a task.
reply: They worked side by side for three years.
replyJapanese: 二人は3年間、肩を並べて働きました。
transferReply: Put the two versions side by side.
transferReplyJapanese: 2つの版を並べて置いてください。
nuance: Fixed word order with no articles. Two senses: physically adjacent, and cooperating.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない固定表現で、語順も変わらない。「隣り合って」と「協力して」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Be acceptable to someone.
japanese: その人にとって、納得がいく。
cue: A decision has made people uneasy.
reply: The change doesn't sit well with the team.
replyJapanese: あの変更は、チームには納得がいかないようです。
transferReply: That version sits well with everyone.
transferReplyJapanese: その案なら、全員が納得しています。
nuance: With introduces the person. Very often negative, as a polite way to report discomfort.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は with で示す。否定形で使うことが非常に多く、不満を穏やかに伝えられる。

meaning: Be missed by a system that should have caught it.
japanese: 仕組みの網の目から、漏れてしまう。
cue: One case was not picked up by a review.
reply: A few cases slipped through the net last year.
replyJapanese: 昨年、いくつかの案件が網から漏れました。
transferReply: The new check stops things slipping through the net.
transferReplyJapanese: 新しい確認で、漏れが起きなくなります。
nuance: British; American English says slip through the cracks. It blames the system, not a person.
nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では slip through the cracks と言う。人ではなく仕組みの問題を示す。

meaning: Say honestly what you think.
japanese: 思っていることを、率直に言う。
cue: A colleague is known for being direct.
reply: She speaks her mind, which I value.
replyJapanese: 彼女は率直に意見を言う人で、そこを買っています。
transferReply: Please speak your mind — this is a draft.
transferReplyJapanese: 率直に言ってください。まだ草案ですから。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually approving, unlike blunt or tactless.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。blunt や tactless と違い、ふつうは肯定的。

meaning: Be a sign that problems are coming.
japanese: 面倒の前触れになる。
cue: An early warning sign has appeared.
reply: Three cancellations in a week spells trouble.
replyJapanese: 1週間に3件の取り消しは、面倒の前触れです。
transferReply: Frost in May spells trouble for the fruit.
transferReplyJapanese: 5月の霜は、果物にとって厄介の前触れです。
nuance: Trouble takes no article. The sign is the subject, and for introduces who is affected.
nuanceJapanese: trouble に冠詞は付かない。主語は兆候のほうで、影響を受ける側は for で示す。

meaning: Exactly right.
japanese: まさにそのとおり。ぴたりと正確。
cue: A colleague's summary captured it exactly.
reply: That summary is spot on.
replyJapanese: その要約は、まさにそのとおりです。
transferReply: The measurements were spot on.
transferReplyJapanese: 寸法は、ぴたりと正確でした。
nuance: British and informal. It follows be or stands alone as a one-word agreement.
nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。be のあとに置くか、単独で同意を示す返事として使う。

meaning: Come into your thoughts immediately.
japanese: ぱっと頭に浮かぶ。
cue: You are asked for an example without warning.
reply: Two examples spring to mind.
replyJapanese: ふたつ、すぐに思い浮かびます。
transferCue: Admit you cannot think of one.
transferReply: Nothing springs to mind, I'm afraid.
transferReplyJapanese: 残念ながら、何も思い浮かびません。
nuance: Spring is irregular: sprang, sprung. The idea is the subject, and mind takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: spring は不規則変化で sprang、sprung。主語は思いつくもので、mind に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: State publicly that you have a right to something.
japanese: 権利があると、はっきり主張する。
cue: Someone put themselves forward for a role early.
reply: She staked a claim to the project in March.
replyJapanese: 彼女は3月に、その企画への意欲を明確に示しました。
transferReply: Both firms have staked a claim to the market.
transferReplyJapanese: 両社とも、その市場に名乗りを上げています。
nuance: To introduces what is claimed. It implies acting early to secure a position.
nuanceJapanese: 主張の対象は to で示す。先んじて立場を確保する含みがある。

meaning: Accept that you were wrong after being told.
japanese: 指摘を受けて、誤りを認める。
cue: Someone corrects a detail you had wrong.
reply: It was 2018? I stand corrected.
replyJapanese: 2018年でしたか。訂正します、失礼しました。
transferReply: I stand corrected on the figure.
transferReplyJapanese: その数字については、私の誤りでした。
nuance: Almost always first person and present tense. Gracious rather than defensive.
nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに一人称の現在形。身構えるのではなく、潔く認める言い方。

meaning: Refuse to change your position under pressure.
japanese: 圧力に屈せず、立場を貫く。
cue: A supplier is pressing for a change of terms.
reply: We should stand firm on the payment schedule.
replyJapanese: 支払い条件については、譲らないほうがいいでしょう。
transferReply: The committee stood firm despite the letters.
transferReplyJapanese: 多くの手紙が来ても、委員会は姿勢を変えませんでした。
nuance: Stand is irregular: stood. On introduces the issue. Firm is an adverb here, not firmly.
nuanceJapanese: stand は不規則変化で stood。争点は on で示す。ここでの firm は副詞で、firmly とは言わない。

meaning: Behave very formally.
japanese: 堅苦しく、形式ばる。
cue: You want a guest to feel relaxed.
reply: Don't stand on ceremony — help yourself.
replyJapanese: 堅苦しくせず、どうぞご自由に取ってください。
transferReply: Nobody stands on ceremony here.
transferReplyJapanese: ここでは、誰も堅苦しくしません。
nuance: Ceremony takes no article. Almost always in the negative, as an invitation to relax.
nuanceJapanese: ceremony に冠詞は付かない。ほぼつねに否定形で、くつろぐよう促す表現。

meaning: Remain where you are.
japanese: その場を動かずにいる。
cue: A group is separating in a crowded place.
reply: Stay put and I'll find you.
replyJapanese: そこを動かないでください。私が探します。
transferCue: Describe a decision not to move house.
transferReply: We've decided to stay put for another year.
transferReplyJapanese: もう1年、今の家にとどまることにしました。
nuance: Put is fixed and does not change. Used for people and for objects that should not move.
nuanceJapanese: put は固定で変化しない。人にも、動かしたくない物にも使う。

meaning: Take responsibility when it is needed.
japanese: 必要な場面で、進んで責任を引き受ける。
cue: Someone volunteered when a leader left.
reply: She stepped up to the plate when he resigned.
replyJapanese: 彼が辞任したとき、彼女が進んで役割を引き受けました。
transferReply: We need someone to step up to the plate.
transferReplyJapanese: 誰かが、進んで引き受けてくれる必要があります。
nuance: From baseball, and mostly American. Plate takes the, and the phrase praises initiative.
nuanceJapanese: 野球由来で主にアメリカ英語。plate には the を付け、自発性をほめる表現。

meaning: Almost do something, but not quite.
japanese: すんでのところで、そこまではしない。
cue: A report criticised without naming anyone.
reply: The review stops short of blaming anyone.
replyJapanese: その検証は、誰かを名指しするまでには至っていません。
transferReply: He stopped short of apologising properly.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はきちんと謝るところまでは行きませんでした。
nuance: Followed by -ing. It marks the limit of an action, often with a note of criticism.
nuanceJapanese: -ing を続ける。行為の限界を示し、批判を含むことが多い。

meaning: Reach an agreement after negotiating.
japanese: 交渉の末に、取引をまとめる。
cue: Two sides agreed after a long discussion.
reply: They struck a deal late on Friday.
replyJapanese: 金曜の遅くに、双方は取引をまとめました。
transferReply: We struck a deal at half the asking price.
transferReplyJapanese: 言い値の半額で、話をまとめました。
nuance: Strike is irregular: struck. With introduces the other party.
nuanceJapanese: strike は不規則変化で struck。相手は with で示す。

phrase: strike while the iron is hot
meaning: Act now, while conditions are favourable.
japanese: 好機のうちに、すぐ動く。
cue: Interest in a proposal is high right now.
reply: Let's strike while the iron is hot and send it today.
replyJapanese: 好機のうちに、今日中に送ってしまいましょう。
transferReply: She struck while the iron was hot and accepted.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は好機を逃さず、その場で受けました。
frame: Strike while the iron is hot
nuance: From blacksmithing. The tense of is follows the sentence, as in while the iron was hot.
nuanceJapanese: 鍛冶に由来。is の時制は文に合わせ、while the iron was hot のようになる。
aliases: strike while the iron was hot

meaning: The obstacle that prevents progress.
japanese: 前に進むのを妨げている、障害。
cue: One issue is holding up an agreement.
reply: Price is the main stumbling block.
replyJapanese: 最大の障害は、価格です。
transferReply: Pronunciation was a stumbling block at first.
transferReplyJapanese: 最初は、発音が壁になりました。
nuance: Countable. It names the single obstacle in the way, not general difficulty.
nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞。漠然とした困難ではなく、行く手をふさぐ具体的な障害を指す。

meaning: Do the opposite of what most people are doing.
japanese: 大勢の流れに、逆らって進む。
cue: Someone holds an unpopular position.
reply: She's swimming against the tide on this one.
replyJapanese: この件で、彼女は流れに逆らっています。
transferCue: Describe a business resisting a trend.
transferReply: The shop swims against the tide and still thrives.
transferReplyJapanese: あの店は流れに逆らいながら、今も繁盛しています。
nuance: Swim is irregular: swam, swum. Tide takes the, and the phrase implies effort, not error.
nuanceJapanese: swim は不規則変化で swam、swum。tide には the を付け、誤りではなく労力を含意する。

meaning: Adopt a strict position and refuse to soften it.
japanese: 強硬な姿勢を取って、譲らない。
cue: An organisation refuses to negotiate on a point.
reply: They take a hard line on late payment.
replyJapanese: 支払い遅延について、彼らは強硬な姿勢です。
transferReply: We'd rather not take a hard line yet.
transferReplyJapanese: 今はまだ、強硬な姿勢は取りたくありません。
frame: Take a hard line on something
nuance: On introduces the issue. Line takes a. It describes policy, not anger.
nuanceJapanese: 争点は on で示す。line には a を付ける。怒りではなく、方針についての表現。

meaning: Start liking someone quickly.
japanese: すぐに、その人を気に入る。
cue: A normally reserved colleague warmed to a newcomer.
reply: He's taken a shine to the new apprentice.
replyJapanese: 彼は新しい見習いを、すっかり気に入ったようです。
transferCue: Describe a cat and a visitor.
transferReply: The cat took a shine to her immediately.
transferReplyJapanese: 猫はすぐに、彼女になつきました。
nuance: Informal and warm. To introduces the person, and it implies the liking was quick.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた温かい表現。相手は to で示し、すぐに好きになったことを含意する。

meaning: Move somewhere safe from danger or weather.
japanese: 危険や雨風から、身を隠す。
cue: A sudden downpour began on a walk.
reply: We took cover under a tree.
replyJapanese: 木の下で、雨宿りしました。
transferCue: Describe a warning at a site.
transferReply: Take cover when you hear the siren.
transferReplyJapanese: サイレンが鳴ったら、安全な場所に避難してください。
nuance: Cover takes no article. Used for weather and for danger alike.
nuanceJapanese: cover に冠詞は付かない。天候にも危険にも使う。

meaning: Feel encouraged by something.
japanese: それを励みにして、気を取り直す。
cue: A difficult period has one positive sign.
reply: We can take heart from the March figures.
replyJapanese: 3月の数字を、励みにできます。
transferCue: Encourage a friend after a setback.
transferReply: Take heart — the second attempt is always easier.
transferReplyJapanese: 気を落とさないで。2回目はいつも楽になります。
nuance: Heart takes no article. From introduces the encouraging thing. The opposite is lose heart.
nuanceJapanese: heart に冠詞は付かない。励みになるものは from で示す。反対は lose heart。

meaning: Make a careful effort to do something well.
japanese: 手間を惜しまず、丁寧にやる。
cue: Someone was unusually careful in their explanation.
reply: She took pains to explain it clearly.
replyJapanese: 彼女は手間を惜しまず、丁寧に説明してくれました。
transferReply: He takes pains over every joint.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はどの継ぎ目にも、丁寧に手をかけます。
nuance: Pains is always plural. To plus a verb, or over plus a noun, introduces the care taken.
nuanceJapanese: pains はつねに複数形。to＋動詞、または over＋名詞で、丁寧にする対象を示す。

meaning: Gradually develop into a recognisable form.
japanese: だんだん、形になってくる。
cue: A plan is becoming clearer.
reply: The proposal is starting to take shape.
replyJapanese: 提案が、少しずつ形になってきました。
transferReply: The extension is taking shape nicely.
transferReplyJapanese: 増築部分が、うまく形になってきています。
nuance: Shape takes no article. Usually in the continuous, since it describes gradual progress.
nuanceJapanese: shape に冠詞は付かない。徐々に進む様子を表すので、ふつう進行形で使う。

meaning: Support one person or group in an argument.
japanese: どちらか一方の側につく。
cue: Two friends have fallen out and both want support.
reply: I'd rather not take sides in this.
replyJapanese: この件では、どちらの味方にもなりたくありません。
transferReply: A good chair doesn't take sides.
transferReplyJapanese: よい議長は、どちらにも肩入れしません。
nuance: Sides is always plural, even when supporting one. In introduces the dispute.
nuanceJapanese: 一方につく場合でも sides はつねに複数形。争いは in で示す。

meaning: Criticise someone firmly for something they did.
japanese: その行いについて、厳しく咎める。
cue: A manager addressed a repeated failure directly.
reply: She took him to task over the missing reports.
replyJapanese: 彼女は報告書の不備について、彼を厳しく咎めました。
transferReply: The article takes the council to task for the delay.
transferReplyJapanese: その記事は、遅延について自治体を厳しく批判しています。
frame: Take someone to task over something
nuance: The person goes between take and to. Over or for introduces the fault. Formal in tone.
nuanceJapanese: 相手は take と to のあいだに置く。理由は over か for で示す。改まった響き。

meaning: The less bad of two poor options.
japanese: どちらも悪いなかで、まだましなほう。
cue: Neither available option is good. Choose anyway.
reply: Waiting is the lesser of two evils.
replyJapanese: 待つほうが、まだましです。
transferReply: We took the lesser of two evils and paid the fee.
transferReplyJapanese: まだましなほうを選んで、手数料を払いました。
nuance: Fixed with the and two. It accepts that neither option is good.
nuanceJapanese: the と two を含む固定表現。どちらもよくないことを前提とする。

meaning: The point when you find out whether something works.
japanese: 結果が分かる、決定的な瞬間。
cue: A repair is about to be tested.
reply: This is the moment of truth — try the switch.
replyJapanese: いよいよ本番です。スイッチを入れてみてください。
transferReply: The moment of truth came with the envelope.
transferReplyJapanese: 封筒を開けるときが、決定的な瞬間でした。
nuance: Always with the. It names a single decisive instant, often with light drama.
nuanceJapanese: つねに the を伴う。決定的な一瞬を指し、やや芝居がかった響きになる。

meaning: What is usual or expected in a situation.
japanese: その場では、当たり前になっていること。
cue: Describe the atmosphere during a busy period.
reply: Long hours were the order of the day that month.
replyJapanese: あの月は、長時間労働が当たり前でした。
transferReply: Jeans are the order of the day here.
transferReplyJapanese: ここでは、ジーンズが当たり前です。
frame: Be the order of the day
nuance: Always with the. It describes what prevails, not a formal rule.
nuanceJapanese: つねに the を伴う。正式な規則ではなく、実際に行き渡っている状態を表す。

meaning: The advantages and disadvantages.
japanese: 利点と欠点の両方。
cue: A decision needs weighing up.
reply: Let's list the pros and cons before Friday.
replyJapanese: 金曜までに、利点と欠点を挙げてみましょう。
transferReply: We went through the pros and cons twice.
transferReplyJapanese: 利点と欠点を、2回検討しました。
frame: Weigh up the pros and cons
nuance: Both words are always plural and in that order. They are short for Latin pro and contra.
nuanceJapanese: どちらもつねに複数形で、語順も固定。ラテン語の pro と contra に由来する。

meaning: Fit together with something else.
japanese: ほかのものと、うまくつながる。
cue: A new finding matches an earlier one.
reply: That ties in with what the survey found.
replyJapanese: それは、調査で分かったこととつながります。
transferReply: The launch ties in with the anniversary.
transferReplyJapanese: 発表は、記念日に合わせてあります。
nuance: Inseparable. Used for evidence that agrees and for events timed together.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。一致する証拠にも、時期を合わせた催しにも使う。

meaning: Repeatedly, on many occasions.
japanese: 何度となく、繰り返し。
cue: A warning has been given many times.
reply: We've said this time and again.
replyJapanese: このことは、何度となく言ってきました。
transferReply: It has worked time and again.
transferReplyJapanese: その方法は、何度も効果を上げてきました。
nuance: Often extended to time and time again. It usually carries mild frustration or emphasis.
nuanceJapanese: time and time again と長くすることも多い。軽いいらだちや強調を伴うことが多い。

meaning: Without achieving anything.
japanese: 何の効果もなく。むだに終わって。
cue: Repeated attempts produced no result.
reply: We called three times, to no avail.
replyJapanese: 3回電話しましたが、むだでした。
transferReply: They searched all evening, to no avail.
transferReplyJapanese: 一晩中探しましたが、見つかりませんでした。
nuance: Formal, usually at the end after a comma. Avail takes no article.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現で、ふつう文末にコンマを添えて置く。avail に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Confronting each other directly as equals.
japanese: 真っ向から、対等に渡り合って。
cue: A small firm competed evenly with a large one.
reply: They went toe to toe with a much bigger rival.
replyJapanese: 彼らははるかに大きい相手と、対等に渡り合いました。
transferReply: The two candidates stood toe to toe all evening.
transferReplyJapanese: 二人の候補は一晩中、真っ向から渡り合いました。
frame: Go toe to toe with someone
nuance: From boxing. With introduces the opponent, and it implies the sides were evenly matched.
nuanceJapanese: ボクシング由来。相手は with で示し、互角であったことを含意する。

meaning: Endure a difficult situation rather than giving up.
japanese: 投げ出さずに、耐え抜く。
cue: A hard period has a few weeks left.
reply: We'll tough it out until the end of term.
replyJapanese: 学期末まで、耐え抜きましょう。
transferCue: Describe finishing a race while injured.
transferReply: She toughed it out and finished.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は耐え抜いて、完走しました。
nuance: Fixed with it. Informal, and it emphasises endurance rather than solving the problem.
nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。くだけた言い方で、解決ではなく耐えることを強調する。

meaning: Locked away securely.
japanese: 厳重に鍵をかけて、しまってある。
cue: Sensitive documents need secure storage.
reply: The originals are under lock and key.
replyJapanese: 原本は、厳重に保管してあります。
transferCue: Describe keeping something safe at home.
transferReply: The spare keys stay under lock and key.
transferReplyJapanese: 予備の鍵は、厳重にしまってあります。
frame: Keep something under lock and key
nuance: Fixed word order with no articles. It emphasises security more than simply being locked.
nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない固定表現で、語順も変わらない。単に施錠する以上の厳重さを示す。

meaning: Paid or stated in advance, or open and direct.
japanese: 前払いで。また、隠さず率直に。
cue: Explain a payment arrangement.
reply: They want half the fee up front.
replyJapanese: 先方は、料金の半額を前払いで求めています。
transferReply: She was up front about the risks.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼女は危険について、隠さず話してくれました。
frame: Pay up front / be up front about something
nuance: Written as one word or two. Two senses: paid in advance, and honest about something.
nuanceJapanese: 1語でも2語でも書く。「前払い」と「率直」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Manage carefully between two opposing risks.
japanese: 両方の危うさのあいだで、慎重に進む。
cue: A policy must be firm but not harsh.
reply: We walk a fine line between clear and unkind.
replyJapanese: 明確さと冷たさのあいだで、慎重に線を引いています。
transferReply: He walks a fine line and usually gets it right.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼は際どい線を歩きますが、たいていは外しません。
frame: Walk a fine line between two things
nuance: Between introduces the two risks. Tread a fine line means the same in British English.
nuanceJapanese: 2つの危うさは between で示す。イギリス英語では tread a fine line とも言う。

meaning: Actually do what you have said you would do.
japanese: 口だけでなく、実際に行動する。
cue: Someone's actions matched their stated values.
reply: He talks the talk and walks the walk.
replyJapanese: 彼は口にするだけでなく、実際に行動しています。
transferReply: They say the right things, but do they walk the walk?
transferReplyJapanese: 言うことは立派ですが、実際に行動しているでしょうか。
nuance: Usually paired with talk the talk. Informal and mostly American in origin.
nuanceJapanese: ふつう talk the talk と対にして使う。くだけた、もとはアメリカ英語の表現。

meaning: Lose something and accept it is gone.
japanese: もう戻らないものとして、あきらめる。
cue: A missed deadline lost an opportunity.
reply: We can wave goodbye to the spring slot.
replyJapanese: 春の枠は、あきらめるしかありません。
transferReply: They waved goodbye to the deposit.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼らは手付金をあきらめました。
nuance: To introduces what is lost. It treats the loss as final, usually with resignation.
nuanceJapanese: 失うものは to で示す。取り返しがつかないものとして、あきらめ気味に使う。

meaning: Cause someone serious and continuing worry.
japanese: 重くのしかかって、悩ませ続ける。
cue: A difficult decision is troubling someone.
reply: The choice weighs heavily on her.
replyJapanese: その選択が、彼女に重くのしかかっています。
transferReply: The responsibility weighed heavily on the whole team.
transferReplyJapanese: その責任は、チーム全体に重くのしかかりました。
nuance: The worry is the subject, and on introduces the person. It describes lasting burden.
nuanceJapanese: 主語は悩みのほうで、人は on で示す。一時的ではなく、続く重荷を表す。

meaning: Having plenty of money, or in a good situation.
japanese: 暮らし向きがよい。恵まれている。
cue: Compare two neighbourhoods.
reply: That part of town is noticeably well off.
replyJapanese: 町のあのあたりは、明らかに裕福です。
transferReply: We don't know how well off we are.
transferReplyJapanese: 自分たちがどれだけ恵まれているか、分かっていません。
nuance: Hyphenated before a noun. Not know when you are well off means failing to see your advantages.
nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前ではハイフンでつなぐ。not know when you are well off は、恵まれていると気づかないこと。

meaning: Young and without experience.
japanese: 経験が浅く、まだ青い。
cue: Describe yourself at the start of a career.
reply: I was wet behind the ears when I started here.
replyJapanese: ここで働き始めたころは、まだ青二才でした。
transferReply: He's a little wet behind the ears but he learns fast.
transferReplyJapanese: 彼はまだ経験が浅いですが、覚えるのは早いです。
nuance: Ears is always plural. Mildly critical, so it is gentler about yourself than about others.
nuanceJapanese: ears はつねに複数形。やや批判的なので、他人より自分について使うほうがやわらかい。

meaning: Get something or someone back after losing them.
japanese: 一度失ったものを、取り戻す。
cue: A customer who left has returned.
reply: We won back two of the accounts.
replyJapanese: 取引先のうち2社を、取り戻しました。
transferReply: It took a year to win back their confidence.
transferReplyJapanese: 信頼を取り戻すまでに、1年かかりました。
nuance: Separable: win it back. Win is irregular: won. It implies the loss came first.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：win it back。win は不規則変化で won。まず失ったことが前提になる。

meaning: Very warmly and willingly.
japanese: 両手を広げて、心から歓迎して。
cue: A returning colleague was warmly received.
reply: The team welcomed her back with open arms.
replyJapanese: チームは彼女を、心から歓迎して迎えました。
transferReply: The idea was received with open arms.
transferReplyJapanese: その案は、両手を広げて受け入れられました。
nuance: Arms is always plural. Usually with welcome or receive, and always positive.
nuanceJapanese: arms はつねに複数形。welcome や receive と使い、つねに肯定的。

meaning: Reach a senior position by starting at the bottom.
japanese: 下から始めて、階段を上っていく。
cue: Describe a colleague's career path.
reply: She worked her way up from the post room.
replyJapanese: 彼女は郵便室から始めて、今の立場に上がりました。
transferCue: Describe an expectation in a trade.
transferReply: Most people work their way up over ten years.
transferReplyJapanese: たいていの人は、10年かけて上がっていきます。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It implies slow progress earned by effort.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。努力で少しずつ上がることを含意する。

meaning: Manage to understand something difficult.
japanese: 難しいことを、なんとかのみこむ。
cue: A new concept is hard to grasp.
reply: I can't quite wrap my mind around the pricing.
replyJapanese: あの料金体系が、どうにものみこめません。
transferReply: It takes a while to wrap your mind around it.
transferReplyJapanese: のみこむまでに、しばらくかかります。
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Head is the more common variant; both are informal.
nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。head を使う形のほうが一般的で、どちらもくだけた表現。

meaning: Not important at all.
japanese: 取るに足らず、重要ではない。
cue: A small discrepancy does not affect anything.
reply: A day either way is of no consequence.
replyJapanese: 1日ずれても、大した問題ではありません。
transferReply: The colour is of no consequence here.
transferReplyJapanese: ここでは、色は問題になりません。
nuance: Formal. Consequence takes no article in this sense, and the phrase follows be.
nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現。この意味では consequence に冠詞は付かず、be のあとに置く。

meaning: Deeply asleep or unconscious.
japanese: ぐっすり眠り込んでいる。
cue: Describe a child after a long day out.
reply: He was out for the count by seven.
replyJapanese: 彼は7時には、ぐっすり眠っていました。
transferCue: Describe yourself after a long journey.
transferReply: I was out for the count within minutes.
transferReplyJapanese: 数分で、私は眠り込んでいました。
nuance: From boxing. British and informal, and usually about deep sleep rather than injury.
nuanceJapanese: ボクシング由来のくだけたイギリス英語。けがではなく、深い眠りについて使う。

meaning: Not something that affects or bothers me.
japanese: 自分には、痛くもかゆくもない。
cue: A change does not affect you either way.
reply: It's no skin off my nose which room we use.
replyJapanese: どちらの部屋でも、私は構いません。
transferCue: Decline to object to a plan.
transferReply: Go ahead — no skin off my nose.
transferReplyJapanese: どうぞ進めてください。私には関係ありません。
frame: Be no skin off my nose
nuance: Informal, and the possessive follows the speaker. It can sound indifferent, so tone matters.
nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、所有格は話し手に合わせる。冷たく響くこともあるので、口調に注意。

meaning: Gain an advantage by acting before others.
japanese: 先手を打って、優位に立つ。
cue: A competitor launched first.
reply: They stole a march on us with the early launch.
replyJapanese: 先行発売で、彼らに先を越されました。
transferReply: We stole a march by booking in January.
transferReplyJapanese: 1月に予約して、先手を打ちました。
nuance: Steal is irregular: stole, stolen. On introduces the rival who was beaten to it.
nuanceJapanese: steal は不規則変化で stole、stolen。先を越された相手は on で示す。

meaning: People or things that are not important compared with others.
japanese: ほかと比べれば、取るに足りない存在。
cue: A minor case sits alongside much larger ones.
reply: Our order is small fry to a supplier that size.
replyJapanese: あの規模の業者にとって、うちの注文は小さなものです。
transferCue: Describe a minor player in a market.
transferReply: They were small fry until the merger.
transferReplyJapanese: 合併までは、彼らは小さな存在でした。
nuance: Uncountable and always plural in form. It compares, so it needs a larger thing in view.
nuanceJapanese: 不可算だが形はつねに複数。比較の表現なので、より大きな対象が前提になる。

meaning: Dismiss an objection without properly considering it.
japanese: 異論を、まともに取り合わずに退ける。
cue: Concerns were raised and ignored.
reply: They swept aside every objection.
replyJapanese: 彼らはすべての異論を、退けてしまいました。
transferReply: The new evidence swept aside the old theory.
transferReplyJapanese: 新しい証拠が、古い説を一掃しました。
nuance: Separable: sweep it aside. Sweep is irregular: swept. Usually critical when used about objections.
nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：sweep it aside。sweep は不規則変化で swept。異論について使うと批判的になる。

meaning: Say things that are reasonable and practical.
japanese: 筋の通った、現実的なことを言う。
cue: One person brought a discussion back to reality.
reply: At last, somebody talking sense.
replyJapanese: やっと、まともなことを言う人が出ました。
transferReply: Talk sense — we can't do it in a day.
transferReplyJapanese: 現実的に考えてください。1日では無理です。
nuance: Sense takes no article. As a command it is blunt, so it suits close colleagues.
nuanceJapanese: sense に冠詞は付かない。命令形はぶっきらぼうなので、親しい相手向き。

meaning: Revealing something that was meant to be hidden.
japanese: 隠していたことを、うっかり示してしまう。
cue: Small signs revealed that someone had been in a room.
reply: There were tell-tale crumbs on the desk.
replyJapanese: 机の上に、それと分かるパンくずが残っていました。
transferReply: The tell-tale rattle started again.
transferReplyJapanese: 例のがたつく音が、また始まりました。
nuance: Hyphenated and used before a noun. Very often with sign or signs.
nuanceJapanese: ハイフンでつなぎ、名詞の前に置く。sign や signs と組み合わせることが非常に多い。
